reviewed_by: Claude Opus 5 blind reviewer, re-review after the object-to-unit pairing fixes, 2026-08-13

samples_reviewed.question_text: A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?

Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.
Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sentence asks for perimeter of a plane figure, yet only six of the sixteen samples ask for a perimeter at all: seeds 42, 43, 46, 601, 603 and 604. Seven samples ask instead for the length of a single unnamed object, for example seed 44 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' and seed 68 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.'. Length of one object is not perimeter of a figure, and as rendered these stems are unanswerable: no object is named, no side lengths are given, and nothing in the packet identifies what is being measured, so the key 14 at seed 44 cannot be recovered from the information given.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sentence names two verbs and a tool clause, and none of the three is exercised. No sample asks the student to identify the perimeter, for instance to pick out the distance around a figure as opposed to the space inside it. No sample names a measuring tool such as a ruler or tape measure; the closest is seed 605 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?', which is about units, not tools, and is a length-and-distance question rather than a perimeter one. Seeds 606 'Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?' and 607 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm.' belong to the same off-node family, so ten of sixteen samples sit outside this competency.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Taken on their own the six genuine perimeter items are pitched correctly for Grade 2 Quarter 4: seed 603 'A square has a side of 3 cm.' answers 12, seed 43 answers 34 from two given sides, and seed 604 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm.' answers 10 by simple addition. Each is a one-step sum of whole numbers well inside Grade 2 range, with no formula notation and no reliance on multiplication beyond repeated addition.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters do appear (mcq at seed 42, cloze at seed 50, read_mcq at seed 68), but the variety is spent on the wrong stems. Within the perimeter items the shapes are reasonable, covering triangle at seed 42, rectangle at seed 43 and square at seed 603, yet seven of sixteen slots are consumed by one repeated template, 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.', which supplies no variety of its own and differs between seeds only in the hidden key. The single word-problem variant, seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 m long and 10 m wide.', is left as the only contextual item.

competency_alignment.rationale: The node pulls content from a neighbouring competency. Seed 605, seed 606 and seed 607 are unit-choice and longer-than comparison items about length and distance, and the seven 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' items measure a single length rather than the distance around a plane figure. Only the six perimeter stems, such as seed 46 'A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm.', map onto the sentence, so the majority of the node addresses a different learning competency than the one it is filed under.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The perimeter figures themselves are sound and their units fit: seed 42 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm.' satisfies the triangle inequality because 1 plus 2 exceeds 2, seed 604 with sides 2, 4 and 4 satisfies it because 2 plus 4 exceeds 4, and seed 601 puts an 11 by 10 garden in metres, which is right for a garden. The measurement items are not sound. Seed 500 keys 409, seed 501 keys 328 and seed 502 keys 259 for a stem that reads 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.'; an object of three to four metres reported to the nearest centimetre is not something a Grade 2 pupil measures with a classroom ruler, and no object able to carry such a size is named. Seed 607 compounds this by placing a bench 22 cm from a tree while seed 605 in the same node teaches that such a distance is measured in 'm'.
